CASE STUDY
HEARTLINK: THE CARDIOLOGIST presents it himself.
A heart attack film presented by an AI clone of Dr Harmandeep Singh, Consultant Cardiologist, made with his consent and carrying the HeartLink brand throughout.

CLIENT
HeartLink
PRESENTER
AI clone of Dr Harmandeep Singh: his face and voice, with consent
MASTER FILM
02:30, 16:9
SHORTS
3 vertical, 9:16
Read the transcript and sources

WHY AN AI PRESENTER
PATIENTS TRUST A FACE THEY WILL meet.
A narrated animation explains. A film presented by the clinician also introduces them. The AI clone gives that presence without a filming day, a studio or a retake every time guidance changes.
The film opens with the cardiologist, moves through the anatomy of a blocked artery and the symptoms to act on, follows one patient from the 999 call to the catheter lab, and closes on a single instruction: call 999.
01
Consent first
The clinician signs a consent form before anything is recorded.
02
One short session
A single recording session captures their face and voice.
03
Their words, approved
The clone only ever says a script the clinician has reviewed and signed off.
04
Used for nothing else
The clone is used only for that client’s approved films, and is deleted on request.
05
Said on screen
The film states that it is presented by an AI avatar, created with the clinician’s consent.

FOR THE FEED
THREE SHORTS FROM one film.
Know the signs. Inside a heart attack. Reopening the artery. Each is a self-contained 30 to 45 seconds with burned-in captions, built to be understood with the sound off.

{"@context":"https://schema.org","@type":"VideoObject","name":"Heart attack: know the signs and act fast","description":"Presented by an AI avatar of Dr Harmandeep Singh, made with his consent: what a heart attack is, the symptoms, calling 999, and how a stent reopens the artery.","thumbnailUrl":"https://www.plainsightmedical.co.uk/media/heart-attack.jpg","contentUrl":"https://www.plainsightmedical.co.uk/media/heart-attack.mp4","uploadDate":"2026-09-21","duration":"PT2M30S","inLanguage":"en-GB","transcript":"A heart attack is a medical emergency. Knowing the signs, and acting fast, can save a life. Your heart pumps oxygen-rich blood from your lungs out to your body, and sends oxygen-poor blood back to your lungs. The heart muscle itself also needs oxygen-rich blood, supplied by its own arteries, the coronary arteries. Over many years, a fatty plaque can build up inside the wall of an artery, covered by a thin fibrous cap. If that cap tears, a blood clot forms on the plaque, and can block the artery. The heart muscle beyond the blockage is starved of oxygen, and begins to be damaged. The most common warning sign is chest pain, or a feeling of pressure or tightness. It can spread to the arms, neck, jaw or back, and you may feel breathless, sweaty or sick. Symptoms aren't the same for everyone. Some people, particularly women, feel breathless or sick, or have back or jaw pain, without chest pain. If you think someone is having a heart attack, call 999 straight away. Don't drive
